_finding: Identity is the issuer registry's exact address; a name only ever claims one. A matcher that flags a registry token as resembling itself calls the real NVDAc an impostor, and one that compares symbols ignoring case promotes every memecoin called `nvda` to the strong claim `registry_symbol`. And on Robinhood the issuer's symbols ARE the bare tickers (GME, COIN, F): a strong grade on an exact symbol match there took in borrowed tickers by the thousand on the first census, so the strong grade requires a distinctive issuer symbol.

mutations.name: a registry token is checked for resemblance to itself
mutations.find: if (!addr || recs.some((r) => r.address === addr)) return null
mutations.expect: FAIL a registry token resembles nothing: it IS the asset

mutations.name: the strong match ignores case
mutations.find: const exact = recs.find((r) => r.symbol === sym && tickerOf(r) !== r.symbol)
mutations.replace: const exact = recs.find((r) => r.symbol.toLowerCase() === sym.toLowerCase() || tickerOf(r).toLowerCase() === sym.toLowerCase())
mutations.expect: FAIL the bare ticker is a weak resemblance

mutations.name: a bare-ticker issuer symbol makes the strong claim
mutations.find: const exact = recs.find((r) => r.symbol === sym && tickerOf(r) !== r.symbol)
mutations.expect: FAIL a bare-ticker issuer symbol (Robinhood GME) is only a weak resemblance
